name: feeler-gap
title: Feeler Gap
description: A machinist's go/no-go gauge for threshold status: a chip sized to the live value slides toward a slot sized to the limit, gliding through with a labeled clearance gap or wedging in the jaws with a damped shudder — the physical gap between chip and slot IS the margin.
useWhen: a threshold check (bundle size vs budget, latency vs SLA, payload vs limit) where the margin itself — not just pass/fail — should be visible in one still frame, rendered as two physical widths on the same scale so the leftover span between chip and jaw reads as headroom without a color-coded badge; pick assay-gate instead for a human approving/editing an agent's proposed arguments, or rule-sparkline for a trend against a rule rather than a single value-vs-limit reading.
instruction: Renders one threshold check — a live `value` against a `limit`, both in the same `unit` — as a physical go/no-go gauge instead of a red/green badge. Two SVG jaw shapes (rounded --muted blocks with a thin --border boundary tick at each inner face) form a fixed-width mouth whose opening always represents `limit` on-scale; a rectangle chip, filled --foreground, is sized to `value` at that identical px-per-unit, so the ratio of the two rendered widths on screen is exactly value/limit no matter the unit (KB, ms, MB, anything). The chip is painted underneath the jaws in SVG paint order, which matters for the jam case (see below). On every value or limit change the chip's x and width ease with a single CSS transition (650ms, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) — ease-out-expo shaped) to its new resting position: if value <= limit the chip glides fully into the mouth and centers between the two jaws, arriving with equal daylight visible on both sides — that visible negative space, doubled as a Geist Mono caption below the gauge ('88 KB clear'), is the clearance, read directly off the same still frame rather than computed from two separate numbers. If value > limit the chip cannot center — it decelerates in only as far as flush against the far jaw's inner face, and because it's painted under the jaws, the portion that overlaps the near jaw's body is occluded there, leaving only the true un-swallowed excess visible as a stub protruding out past the near jaw's outer edge; the resting width itself is 2px narrower than the raw overshoot geometry (the 'compresses 2px' squeeze), and once that arrival transition finishes a CSS keyframe animation nudges the whole chip through a decaying three-swing horizontal shudder (480ms, six keyframe stops alternating and shrinking in amplitude) before settling — replayed via a remount key every time a fresh value lands in a jam, including on first mount, so a gauge that starts over-limit demonstrates itself without waiting for a prop change. The caption in that state reads '24 KB over' instead. Pass/fail is never carried by the jam animation alone: a Geist Mono CLEAR/OVER token (foreground ink, OVER additionally bold, each with its own inline glyph — a check or a broken tick mark, never a color swap) sits directly beside the label at the top of the gauge and is present at rest in both states. Structurally this is a passive meter, not a control: the gauge itself is `role=meter`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label, `aria-valuemin=0`, `aria-valuemax` = limit, `aria-valuenow` = value (deliberately allowed to exceed valuemax when over budget — that excess is the entire point of the reading), and `aria-valuetext` spells the full sentence ('412 KB of 500 KB budget, 88 KB clearance' or '...36 KB over') so assistive tech gets the same margin sighted users read off the gap; a visually-hidden `role=status`/`aria-live=polite` paragraph mirrors that same text so a value change is announced without the meter needing focus. The SVG itself is aria-hidden — decorative once the meter node carries the real semantics — and, being a pure display component with no exposed control, is correctly exempt from any Tab-reachability expectation. Every stroke and fill in the gauge is `fill-current`/`stroke-current` colored by a `text-muted` / `text-foreground` / `text-border` class, never a numeric color literal, so both themes restyle for free. Under prefers-reduced-motion (checked via matchMedia with a change listener, plus a belt-and-suspenders CSS media block) the chip's transition and the shudder keyframe animation are both stripped entirely — a value or limit change snaps straight to the final resting position, fully legible either way, just without the glide or the wiggle. Differs from assay-gate (a human approving and editing an agent's proposed tool-call arguments, collapsing once into an audit receipt) and from rule-sparkline (a KPI trend line over time against a rule) by having no history and no decision at all — it is a single instant's value-vs-limit reading, and the entire mechanism is two widths on one scale rendering their own margin as visible daylight, legible from a single still frame with no legend required.
